newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-BASTIA BEAT MARSEILLE IN MATCH OF PAINFUL MEMORIES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BASTIA BEAT MARSEILLE IN MATCH OF PAINFUL MEMORIES.

text.p: Bruised Bastia took some comfort from an 2-0 home win over former European champion Marseille in a match that triggered painful memories at the Furiani stadium on Sunday.
The two sides had not met since their May 1992 Cup semi-final which turned into a nightmare when 17 people were killed and over 2,000 injured after a temporary platform collapsed before the kick-off.
The Sunday match originally scheduled on Friday was postponed for 48 hours because of security reasons. The stadium has been cordoned off by over 400 policemen.
After a tense beginning, the Corsicans confirmed their ambitions when defender Lubomir Moravcik beat German goalkeeper Andres Koepke in the 17th minute.
Newly promoted Marseille tried to reply through their Irish goalscorer Tony Cascarino but he headed wide on the best chance 15 minutes before the break.
On the contrary, Croatian striker Anton Drobnjak did not miss the opportunity in the 43rd when he beat Koepke at close range by converting a cross from the right.
Drobnjak moved to the top of the scorers tables with four goals.
